GROUNDS OF APPLICATION AND DETAILS OF DECISION SOUGHT
PART A — STATUTORY AND RULE FRAMEWORK
A.1 Jurisdiction and Power
This application is made pursuant to Sections 536, $39, 541, 545, and 580 of the Industrial Relations Act
2016 (Qld); Rules 8, 49, 64C, 64D, 64E, 64F, and 226 of the Industrial Relations (Tribunals) Rules 2011
(Qld); and the Commission's inherent jurisdiction to control its own processes and prevent abuse of process.
PART B — THE FOUR BINDING GROUNDS
GROUND 1: THE MAHAFFEY ESTOPPEL — THE SECTION 32(5)(a) DEFENCE IS LEGALLY
UNAVAILABLE
B.1.1 The Binding Statutory Findings (Exhibit B1, pp 25-27)
The Regulator’s own Review Officer, Ms Victoria Squires, made three express findings of fact in the Review
Decision dated 24 October 2024:
Finding A: "the rostering of these two shifis amounted to unreasonable management action given that it
was in direct contradiction to the award and the 8-hour agreement."
Finding B: “work events were the sole cause" of the psychological injury.
Finding C: "there was no pre-existing factor or condition."
Page 1 of 9
These are the Regulator's own findings. They are not findings the Respondent can now litigate around.
B.1.2 The Governing Authority: Workers’ Compensation Regulator v Mahaffey ICQ 10
In Workers' Compensation Regulator v Mahaffey ICQ 10 (Martin J, President), the Industrial Court of
Queensland considered the proper application of ss 32(1) and 32(5) of the Workers' Compensation and
Rehabilitation Act 2003 (Qld).
Martin J held at that in considering s 32(5), “after weighing up all the relevant factors", conduct that does
not, on balance, displace the evidence in favour of the worker must result in a finding in the worker's favour.
His Honour emphasised that s 32(1) "covers the whole gamut of the employment relationship" while s 32(5)
is "concerned only with a 'slice' of the employment."
Critically, Martin J endorsed the principle from Bird vy Commonwealth that where two constructions of
workers' compensation legislation are possible, "that which is favourable to the worker should be
preferred” — the foundational canon of beneficial construction.
Application to WC/2024/227:
The Respondent's own Review Officer found that the 17-18 March 2024 rostering was "in direct
contradiction to the award." This is an objective breach of an industrial instrument — not a matter of
managerial judgment or discretion. A roster that contravenes a binding Award cannot, as a matter of law,
constitute "reasonable management action taken in a reasonable way" for the purposes of s 32(5)(a).
The Respondent has advanced no fresh evidence, no materially changed circumstances, and no application to
adduce new evidence to displace this binding finding.
B.1.3 The Contradictory Pleading (Form 9C, para 36)
Despite the above, the Respondent's Statement of Facts and Contentions at paragraph 36 pleads:
"any management action involved in the causation of any injury to the Appellant was reasonable
management action taken in a reasonable way."
This pleading:

e a) directly contradicts the Review Officer's binding factual finding.

*  (b) is legally irreconcilable with Mahaffey ICQ 10.

* (c) constitutes an abuse of process within Rule 226(2)(c) of the Jndustrial Relations (Tribunals)

Rules 2011 (Qid); and
¢ (d) constitutes continuing a procccding "without reasonable cause" within s 545(2)(a)(i) of
the Industrial Relations Act 2016 (Qld).
The Commission is respectfully invited to strike out paragraph 36 of Form 9C.
GROUND 2: THE CHURCH/WICKS BAR — THE UNPLEADED ADHD/ANXIETY AMBUSH IS
PROHIBITED
B.2.1 The Impermissible Late Issue (AR, para 32)
At paragraph 32 of the Admissions Response, the Respondent deploys --- for the first time in this entire
proceeding — an unpleaded causation defence:
Page 2 of 9
“the records show a past medical history of Anxiety and ADHD from 26 October 2022 which is missing
from Exhibit A5."
This issue:

« was never raised during the statutory review process before Review Officer Squires.

* was never pleaded in Form 9C (SOFAC, filed 22 July 2025).

« was not raised for seven months after the medical records were obtained on 8 July 2025.

« was deployed through an Admissions Response — a mechanism carrying no obligation to provide

particulars, supporting evidence, or leave to amend; and

e directly contradicts the Review Officer's express finding of "no pre-existing factor or condition."
B.2.2 The Governing Authorities
Church v Simon Blackwood (Workers' Compensation Regulator) JCQ 031 (Martin J, President):
Martin J held that the lodging of an appeal "does not open the gates for both parties to request the
Commission to determine any number of preliminary issues” and that the ambit of the hearing is determined
by the case before the Regulator. Issues "removed in time and effect" from the review decision cannot be
raised.
Wicks vy Workers' Compensation Regulator QIRC 001 (Merrell DP):
Applying Church, the Deputy President dismissed the Regulator's attempt to raise a limitation period that
was not the subject of the review decision, holding that "the appeal provisions do not contemplate another
issue, removed in time and effect from the review decision, being considered in the appeal."
The October 2022 ADHD/Anxiety issue is precisely the species of issue Church and Wicks prohibit.
B.2.3 The Fruit of the Poisonous Tree
The ADHD/Anxiety material was derived exclusively from medical records obtained in admitted breach of
Rule 64C (Ground 3 below). The issue exists in this proceeding only because of that procedural breach. Even
if the Church/Wicks bar did not apply (which it does), the material is independently inadmissible as the direct
product of unlawfully obtained evidence.

B.3.3 Fraus Omnia Corrumpit and the "But-For" Causation of the Form 9C _
The Respondent's email of 14 July 2025 bypassing the Appellant's then-solicitors (Saines Legal) to secure an
extension of time constitutes fraud by concealment (fraus omnia corrumpit).
1. The Concealment: The Respondent deliberately suppressed the fact that it had already seized the
Appellant's complete medical file on 8 July 2025 (AR para 24) without the mandatory Form 29 service.
2. The "But-For" Causation: But for this active concealment, Saines Legal would have been alerted to the
Rule 64C breach prior to the crystallisation of the Form 9C. Saines Legal would have exercised the
Appellant's statutory right to object under Rule 64E, triggering an automatic stay under Rule 64F.
3. The Consequence: Because of the concealment, the Appellant was deprived of his legal representation
(which broke down upon the subsequent service of the unredacted file on 22 July 2025), and the Respondent
was permitted to file a Form 9C constructed entirely from unlawfully obtained medical intelligence and ex
parte coordination with PID subjects. Submission: A pleading secured through procedural fraud is an abuse
of process. The Form 9C is the fruit of the poisonous tree and must be struck out in its entirety pursuant to
Rule 226(2}(c).

reckless; and (c) admission would be unfair or contrary to public policy.

GROUND 4: PUBLIC INTEREST DISCLOSURE REPRISAL— THE ENTIRE DEFENCE
STRATEGY IS TAINTED
B.4.1 The Foundational Admission (AR, para 20)
At paragraph 20, the Respondent provides an unqualified admission that the Appellant's complaint to the
Ethical Standards Unit was determined on 24 December 2024 to constitute a valid Public Interest
Disclosure under the Public Interest Disclosure Act 2010 (Qld), Reference 24-ESU-1130, naming Ms
Tammy Reese and Ms Chloe Taylor as subjects.
This admission was conspicuously made without the "does not admit because the appeal is a hearing de
novo" qualifier the Respondent deployed at AR paragraphs 2, 34, and 44. The selective omission of the de
novo qualification at the one paragraph that damages the Respondent's case most was a considered forensic
choice. The PLD is an immovable admitted fact.
B,4.2 The Detriment — Exhibit E1 Subpoenaed Email Chain
The objective timeline of ex parte coordination between Ms Matheson, the formally admitted PID subjects,
and Queensland Health HR management is set out in full at Section 4.2 of the Affidavit of C. Shepherd.
B.4.3 The Consequential Legal Effect on s 32(5)
Section 45(2) of the PID Act provides that a manager may take reasonable management action only if the
manager's reasons for taking the action do not include the fact that the employee has made the public interest
disclosure.
Management action that constitutes statutory reprisal under s 40 of the PID Act cannot, as a matter of law,
simultaneously constitute "reasonable management action taken in a reasonable way" under s 32(5)(a) of
the Workers’ Compensation and Rehabilitation Act 2003 (Qld). A statutory prohibition cannot simultaneously
be "reasonable." The s 32(5)(a) exclusion is therefore defeated on this ground independently of Mahaffey.
PART C — RULE 49 VIOLATIONS: THE ADMISSIONS RESPONSE IS SYSTEMATICALLY
DEFECTIVE
C,1 Violation 1 — The Forensic Impossibility (AR paras 24 and 29)
Page 5 of 9
Ms Matheson admits at paragraph 24 that the medical records were "printed on 8 July 2025," She then
asserts at paragraph 20 that "the medical records were not in the possession of the Regulator at the time
of sending the email on 14 July 2025."
These two statements are mutually exclusive. Records printed on 8 July 2025 either were or were not in the
Regulator's possession on 14 July 2025. Both cannot be true. Placing a forensic impossibility on a formal
tribunal record constitutes an abuse of the Commission's processes.
C.2 Violation 2 — Denying Incontrovertible Documentary Contents (AR para 2)
The Appellant sought admission that the Review Decision states the rostering constituted "unreasonable
management action." Ms Matheson responds that she “does not admit the fact ... because the appeal is a
hearing de novo." The Appellant did not ask whether the finding is binding — he asked whether the Review
Decision contains those words. The answer is yes. The words are un the pugs. Under Fox v Percy (2003)
214 CLR 118, contemporaneous documents must be preferred over subjective denials and cannot be "not
admitted" as to their literal contents.
C.3 Violation 3 — Weaponised Vexatious Assertion (AR para 26)
The Appellant sought admission that bowel medications, sexual function treatments, and STI screening
results in Exhibit A5 are irrelevant to a June 2024 psychological injury claim. Ms Matheson "denies" this,
asserting the records "read as a whole, are relevant in that they tend to prove or disprove an allegation in the
proceeding."
No forensic pathway is identified. No allegation is specified. There is no legitimate connection between
hemorrhoid cream, bowel medication, or prostate pathology and a psychiatric injury claim arising from an
Award roster breach, This assertion constitutes a formal written declaration of intent to weaponize
scandalous intimate medical material against a self-represented worker, in violation of s 25 of the Human
Rights Act 2019 (Qid).
PART D — SPOLIATION OF EVIDENCE AND ADVERSE INFERENCES
D.1 Admitted Destruction — Communications Book (AR, para 11(a))
The Respondent admits at AR paragraph 11(a) that Ms Chloe Taylor removed pages from the workplace
Communications Book. Ms Taylor referred to it as a “burn book" in a 6 June 2023 email (Exhibit H).
The Communications Book is a public record within the meaning of s 2 of the Public Records Act
2002 (Qid). Removal of pages constitutes unauthorised disposal contrary to s 13 of that Act.
D.2 Active Suppression — Email Archive Cancellation
Between 5-8 August 2025, the Appellant lodged IT Service Request QH-RITM1 6413751 with Queensland
Health to restore email archives containing contemporaneous evidence of management's knowledge of the
roster breach. The restoration request was cancelled by the department — not passive loss, but affirmative
cancellation.

E.2 Application
A representative who must personally defend her own procedural conduct to avoid disciplinary sanction
cannot simultaneously provide the Commission with objective, unconflicted advice. ‘The Admissions
Response serves not the Regulator's institutional interest, but the personal defensive interests of Ms
Matheson, Ms Reese, and Ms Taylor. This is precisely the disqualifying conflict Kallinicos v Hunt was
designed to address.
E.3 The Section 530 Objection
If the Respondent secks leave for legal representation under s 530(4) of the industrial Relations Act
2016 (Qld), the Appellant formally objects. Any Counsel instructed by Ms Matheson receives instructions
from a conflicted officer whose personal interest taints every instruction. Leave should be refused until
carriage is re-assigned to an independent officer.
PART F — ORDERS SOUGHT
ORDER 1 — PERMANENT EXCLUSION OF EXHIBIT AS5 (Bunning v Cross)
That the medical records obtained pursuant to Form 29 dated 4 July 2025 (Exhibit A5), and all copies
thereof, be permanently excluded from evidence and struck from the Commission's record.
ORDER 2 — PROHIBITION OF UNPLEADED PRE-EXISTING CONDITION DEFENCE
That the Respondent be strictly prohibited from advancing any causation defence alleging a pre-existing
psychological condition, including the "Anxiety and ADHD from 26 October 2022" deployed at AR
paragraph 32.
ORDER 3 — STRIKE OUT OF CONTRADICTORY PLEADING (Mahaffey Estoppel)
That paragraph 36 of the Respondent's Form 9C — and any submission asserting that the relevant
management action was "reasonable management action taken in a reasonable way" -— be struck out
pursuant to Rule 226(2)(c) as an abuse of process.
ORDER 4 — DECLARATION OF STATUTORY PID REPRISAL AND PRECLUSION OF
SECTION 32(5)
That the Commission make a formal Declaration and Finding that the Respondent's conduct between 30 June
and 10 July 2025 — specifically the ex parte coordination with Ms Tammy Reese and Ms Chloe Taylor (the

That Ms Renee Matheson be immediately removed from carriage of this matter and the Respondent be
